translations.text: When the priest is preparing to celebrate the liturgy, he shall say this prayer:
O God, at this my entrance into the holy temple of your glory, make your servants worthy to glorify your holy name.
For you are a merciful God who loves humankind, and to you we offer up glory, to the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, now.
Prayer of the setting forth [of the offering] upon the bosporos [?]: O Lord, who gives life and bestows every good thing, who has given people the hope of eternal life, our Lord and God Jesus Christ,
make us worthy of your holiness, and to accomplish this divine service to you, for the enjoyment of the good things prepared, so that we may be kept by your power at all times,
and may offer up glory to you, to the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, now and always and for ever and ever. Amen.
Second prayer, over the chalice: O Lord our God, who has called us to the true light that enlightens every person coming into the world,
be merciful to our sins and forgive us our transgressions, and make us worthy to serve your holy mysteries.
For you reign, Father and Son and Holy Spirit, now and always and for ever and ever. Amen.
When he covers the parekeli [?], he shall say this prayer:
O Lord our God, who gave the heavenly bread as food for all the faithful, our Lord Jesus Christ, your only-begotten Son,
whom you sent down from heaven for our life, through whom you willed our salvation and redemption, through whom you have blessed us [?] and made us holy:
bless this [offering] set forth here, and receive it upon your heavenly altar as a sacrifice, as a spiritual fragrance, pleasing to you, as a mystery.
Since you are merciful and love humankind, remember all who have brought this offering.
And grant us everything we ask for our salvation; let it not be for our torment,
nor for judgment and the conviction of sins, but for eternal salvation.
Prayer of vesting: You who put on light as a garment, appeared on earth in inexpressible humility and lived among people;
you became our high priest forever after the order of Melchizedek;
you who adorned your Church with truth, O Lord Almighty, grant us the heavenly garment of incorruption.
By your grace, make me, who now approach this divine heavenly service, worthy,
so that I may strip off all defilement like a soiled garment. Adorn my soul with radiance and my body with holiness.
Remove my prayers [?] from me, and scatter my lawless deeds from me. Clothe me with virtue, holiness
and steadfastness, so that, clothed by you with the grace of the priesthood, I may be worthy to enter your sanctuary together with those who kept your holy commandments without stumbling,
and that I may be found at the heavenly wedding feast with the wise and holy virgins, to sing your glory, Christ our God, who took away the sins of all people. For
you, our God, are the one who sanctifies our souls and bodies, and to you we offer up glory, together with the Father and the Holy Spirit, now and always and for ever and ever. Amen.
Prayer over the incense. The deacon shall say the litany; the priest shall recite this prayer.
O good Lord of all and Creator of all created things: accept the offering which these people offer to you through your Christ;
and from your Church grant to each one that benefit, and guide all to the attainment of perfection, and make us worthy of your grace and holiness;
for you are a merciful God who loves mankind, and to you we offer glory, to the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, now and always and to the ages of ages. Amen.
Third prayer over the incense: You who accepted the offering of Abel, of Noah, of Abraham, of Aaron,
of Samuel, of Zechariah — the incense [?] — accept from the hands of us sinners this incense as a sweet savour.
Grant forgiveness for our sins, for blessed and holy and glorious is the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, now and always and to the ages of ages. Amen.
Third prayer: O God Almighty, Lord of great name, grant us the grace to enter the Holy of Holies.
Through the coming of your only-begotten Son we ask and entreat you, for we are afraid and trembling, we who are prepared to stand before your awesome and glorious altar.
Send down upon us your good grace, give life to our souls and bodies, and strengthen our minds in the orthodox faith,
so that with a pure heart we may offer the offering, given from the fruits of the earth, for the forgiveness of our sins and for the propitiation of all your people, by the grace
and mercy and love for mankind of Christ, with whom glory befits you, together with the Holy Spirit, now and always and to the ages of ages. Amen.
Prayer before the "Holy God"
Holy are you, O our God, who dwell among the holy ones and sit upon the thrones of glory.
Holy are you, O our God, who are worshipped and glorified by the holy angels and archangels and by all the powers of heaven.
Holy are you, O our God, who receive the thrice-holy hymn from the six-winged cherubim and seraphim.
Accept from us also, your unworthy servants, the thrice-holy hymn, and have mercy on us.
Ekphonesis: For you are holy, O our God, and you rest among the holy ones; we offer the thrice-holy hymn to the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, now and always and to the ages of ages.
The people: Amen.
They shall say the "Holy God".
Prayer after the "Holy God". Merciful, compassionate, long-suffering, abundant in mercy and true, O Lord,
look down from your prepared dwelling place and deliver us from every temptation of the devil and of men,
and do not withdraw your help from us, for we are not able to overcome those who assail us.
But you are able to rescue us from all who attack us.
Save us, O Lord our God, from all the adversaries of this world by your sweetness,
so that we may enter your holy temple with holy thoughts and carry out your pleasing service, so that we may be made worthy of eternal life,
for yours is the kingdom, the power and the glory, of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, now and always and to the ages of ages. Amen.
The priest shall make the sign of the cross and say: Peace to all.
The people shall say: And with your spirit.
Deacon: A Psalm of David. Let us attend.
The reading, and after it the Alleluia. A Psalm of David. Let us attend.
Prayer of the incense: You are full of all fragrance and goodness, Christ our God, and we offer this incense from what you have given, and we beseech you:
may it come before you from the hands of us poor ones as a sweet fragrance, for the forgiveness of our sins,
for glory befits you, together with the Father and the Holy Spirit, now and always and to the ages of ages. Amen.
After the Alleluia, the litany [?: ქ].
Prayer of the Gospel: We thank you, Lord, who made light shine out of darkness and opened the eyes of our minds
to look upon your commandments, to open our mouths to confess our sins, and to be trained in your commandments. You, Lord,
accept the prayer of your sinful and unworthy servants, and do not disregard our supplication, but in accordance with your great goodness protect
those who have come and those who are about to come to pray with us, and make the light of your divine words shine in our hearts and in theirs.
Aloud: For you are the bringer of good news and the enlightener, the resurrection and the life of our souls and bodies, our God,
and we offer up glory to you, the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, now and always and to the ages of ages.
The people: Amen.
Deacon: Stand upright.
Priest: Peace to all.
The people: And with your spirit.
Priest: [The prayer] of [bowing] the head [?].
Deacon: Let us attend. After the Gospel, the deacon [says] the litany, eight petitions, and "The hour that has come" [?].
The priest shall say this prayer: O God, who have let us hear your divine words,
make our souls wise and enlighten them to understand the spiritual wisdom that has just been read, so that we may not be only hearers of these life-giving commandments of yours,
but doers of good works, and may strive in faith with a guileless soul and a spotless life.
Prayer 2. O Lord, giver of life and of good things, who gave humankind the hope of blessed eternal life,
our Lord Jesus Christ, [?] us to perform this divine service in holiness, for the delight of the blessedness to come.
Aloud: Through Christ Jesus our Lord, with whom glory is fitting to you, together with your life-giving and holy Spirit, now and always and to the ages of ages.
People: Amen.
Priest: Peace.
People: And with your spirit.
Deacon: Our heads…
People: To you, O Lord.
The priest shall say this prayer: Send down, O Lord our God, mercy upon these who have bowed their heads and await the blessing that comes from you.
Shepherd your people, bless your inheritance, and grant to us all that we may think on what is yours [?], speak what is yours every day, and walk in your commandments.

Aloud: That we may always be guarded by your power and attain to the knowledge of your truth, and we offer glory to you, Father, Son and Holy Spirit, now and always and to the ages of ages. People: Amen. 2
3. Deacon: Sing in peace. And they shall say the [hymn/prayer] of the washing of hands.
The deacon shall say: Let no one who is weak, no one who is unworthy, no one who is unable [remain]; but look to yourselves, and stand upright, all of you.
After the bringing in of the holy gifts the deacon shall say: Wisdom! Be attentive [?]. And they shall say the Creed.
The priest shall say it along with them. He shall make the sign of the cross three times, from the words "was crucified" to "with the Father and the Son" [?]. After the Creed the deacon shall say:
Let us stand well, let us all be attentive; let us pray to the Lord together.
People: Kyrie eleison.
The priest shall say this prayer of faith: None of us who are bound by the desires of the flesh is worthy to approach and stand before you, or to serve you, the King of glory.
For serving you is great and fearful, and beyond the reach even of the heavenly powers;
but in your inexpressible love for humankind and your goodness you became man, without sin and without change, and became our High Priest,
and you, as Lord of all, gave us the service of this bloodless sacrifice, for you rule over heaven and earth and the underworld.
You who sit on the throne of the cherubim, Lord of the seraphim, King of Israel, who alone are holy and rest among the holy:
we ask you, who are so good and who answer so graciously: look upon me,
this useless and unworthy servant of yours, and by the power of your Holy Spirit make me, unworthy as I am, worthy,
me who have been clothed with the grace of the priesthood, to stand before this holy table of yours and to perform the priestly service over your spotless body and your true blood.
To you I have bowed my neck, and I beseech you: do not turn your face away from me, O Lord, O Lord,
and do not set me apart from your servants, but be pleased to accept this offering of your sinful and unworthy servant.
For you are the one who offers and is offered, who receives and is received, and who is given to people, O Christ our God,
and to you we offer glory, together with your Father who is without beginning and with the life-giving Holy Spirit, now and always and to the ages of ages. Amen.
Before the kiss of peace, the priest shall say this prayer (2): You who are God and Lord of all, O lover of mankind, make us, who are unworthy, worthy of this hour,
so that, cleansed of all deceit and double-mindedness, we may be united with one another by the holy kiss, joined together by the firm bond of love and peace,
and established in the knowledge of your Godhead, through the holiness of our Lord God and Saviour Jesus Christ.
Aloud: For you are the God of peace, of love and of love for mankind, and to you we offer glory, Father, Son and Holy + Spirit, now and always and to the ages of ages.
The people: Amen.
The priest: Peace + to all.
The people: And with your spirit. The deacon shall say: Let us kiss one another with holy love. The deacon: Let us bow our heads to the Lord.
The people: To you, O Lord.
The priest shall say this prayer: You who alone are Lord, merciful God, [look upon] those who have now bowed their necks before your holy altar and ask for the spiritual gift that comes from you;
send down your blessing and bless them all with spiritual blessing, you who dwell on high and look upon the lowly.
Aloud: For praised and worshipped is your holy name, of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, now and always and to the ages of ages.
The people: Amen.
The deacon shall bow down and say: Kyrie eleison. The priest shall make the sign of the cross and say to him: May the Lord accept your ministry.
The deacon shall recite the general litany, and only this [addition]: And for this holy, glorious, spotless sacrifice set forth and prepared to be offered,
and for those who have brought it, and for the honoured priest who stands here worthily offering it, let us all beseech the Lord God.
The people: Kyrie eleison (three times). The priest shall say these prayers while the deacon is reciting the general litany:
Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, good will among men.
He shall say it three times +++. O Lord, open my lips, and my mouth shall declare your praise. Three times +++.
Fill our mouth with praise, O Lord, that we may sing of your glory, and all the day of your great majesty.
Three times +++. To the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, now and always and to the ages of ages. Amen.
The priest shall say this prayer for himself: You who have looked upon us with mercy and compassion, O Lord, O Lord Almighty, grant us boldness,
…of your poor and unworthy servants, to stand before your holy altar [?: 'გ დ', probably an abbreviation] and to offer to you this rational and bloodless sacrifice for our sins.
Look upon me, your useless servant, and blot out my faults by your mercy, and purify my lips and my heart from every defilement of soul and body.
And remove from me every unseemly and senseless thought. And make me able, by the power of your Holy Spirit, for this service.
And have mercy on me, out of your beneficence, as I draw near before your holy altar.
And be pleased, Lord, that the offering which I offer with my hand may be acceptable, with forgiveness in view of my weakness,
and do not cast me away from your face, Lord, and do not count my unworthiness as defilement, but have mercy on me,
Lord, and by your great mercy and your many compassions drive away my iniquities,
so that, having come without condemnation before your glory, I may be made worthy of the refreshment [?] of your only-begotten Son.
And so that I may not proclaim freedom [?] to others and give this [?], through your boundless love for humankind,
while I myself, as a slave of sin, am found useless. Yes, Master, almighty Lord, hear my supplication, for you are
the one who gives help to all, and we all ask for the mercy that comes from you, from the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, now and always and to the ages of ages. Amen.
Second prayer of Basil. Lord our God, who created us and brought us into this life and showed us the way of eternal
life, and granted us the revelation of the heavenly mystery, and appointed us to that service by the power of your Holy Spirit: be pleased,
Lord, completely, that the service of the new covenant, of your holy mysteries, may be acceptable from us.
Accept our approach before your holy altar in your great mercy, that we may be made worthy to bring to you this bloodless and rational sacrifice,
to offer it for our sins, which you have accepted on your holy and invisible, glorious heavenly altar as a sweet fragrance,
and send down upon us the grace of your Holy Spirit, and may it abide upon us at this hour.
Great and glorious God, incline your ear and hear me, this sinner, and accept this holy offering, as you accepted the sacrifice of Abel,
the offering of Noah, the whole fruit-offering [?] of Abraham, the priesthood and holiness of Moses and Aaron, the complete repentance of David.
And as you accepted this true service from the hands of the holy apostles, so also accept this sacrifice from the hands of us sinners in your kindness,
Lord, that we may be made worthy to stand blameless before your holy altar, and that we may find grace with those wise holy virgins on that terrible day,
when you render justice to each according to their deeds. Through the mercy and love for humankind of Christ, your only-begotten Son,
with whom you are blessed, together with your all-holy, good and life-giving Holy Spirit, now and always and to the ages of ages. Amen.
The third prayer of James, the apostle and brother of the Lord: O God, who in your inexpressible and endless love for mankind sent your only-begotten Son into the world,
so that he might bring back to you once more the sheep that had gone astray: do not turn away from us, O Lord, who have set our hands to offering this awesome and bloodless sacrifice,
for we do not trust in our own righteous deeds but in your mercies, through which you care for our race.
We beseech and pray to your goodness that what has been prepared here may not bring condemnation on your people,
this mystery which you have ordained for our salvation, but that it may be for the blotting out of sins and the renewal of soul and body, so that we may be pleasing to you.
Aloud: By the grace and mercy and love for mankind of your only-begotten + Son,
with whom you are blessed, together with your all-holy, good and life-giving Holy Spirit, now and always and to the ages of ages.
People: Amen.
Priest: Peace + to all.
People: And to your spirit. The deacons are to lift up the veil, and the one on the right is to say: Let us stand well, let us stand attentively, let us stand with fear.
Look upon this holy offering, for we are offering the sacrifice of God.
People: Mercy, peace, a sacrifice of praise. [?]
[?] The priest is to say this prayer, bowing: O good Lord who loves mankind, who through the coming of your only-begotten Son,
through his being with us, and through the help of your all-holy and life-giving Holy Spirit,
have made us worthy to stand before your holy altar, to serve the immortal mysteries of the new covenant.
Show us a good sign, and make us worthy, O Good One, to serve you with a pure heart all the days of our life, in the love of holiness, for the sake of your holy name.
The second prayer. O Lord, eternal King and Creator of the ages, great and glorious God, incline your ear at this hour and hear me,
this sinner, and accept this holy offering set before you, just as you accepted the sacrifice of Abel, the offering of Noah,
the whole burnt offering of Abraham, the priesthood of Moses and Aaron, the peace offering of Samuel, the complete repentance of David,
the incense of Zechariah; and just as you accepted this true service from the hands of the holy apostles, so now too, O Lord, you are the same God.
Have mercy on us for the sake of your holy name.
Aloud: The love of God the Father +, the grace of the Lord God, our Redeemer and Saviour Jesus Christ +, and the communion of the All-Holy + be with you all.
People: And with your spirit. Priest: Let your hearts be on high. People: We have them with the Lord. Priest: Let us give thanks to the Lord.
People: It is fitting and right.
The priest is to say this prayer: And since it is truly fitting and right and seemly, and we are bound to praise you, to sing hymns to you, to bless you,
To you be the proclamation of glory, to you worship, to you thanksgiving, who are the Creator of all created things, visible and invisible,
the treasure of eternal good things, who are the fountain of life for all, God and Lord, to whom the heavens sing, and the heavens of heavens, and all their powers,
the sun and the moon and all the orders of the stars, the earth, the sea and everything that is in it, Jerusalem, the assembly of the church of the firstborn
who are written in the heavens, the spirits of the righteous and of the prophets, the souls of the apostles and of the martyrs, angels, archangels, thrones,
dominions, principalities, authorities and powers, the many-eyed cherubim and the six-winged seraphim, who with two wings cover their faces,
with two wings cover their feet, and with two they fly, crying out one to another with unceasing lips and never-silent hymns of God.
Exclamation: With radiant voice they sing, call out, cry aloud and say the hymn of victory to the glory of your great majesty.
People: Holy +, holy +, holy + Lord of Sabaoth. Heaven and earth are full of his glory. Save us,
you who are in the highest. Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord. Save us, you who are in the highest.
Let the priest say this + prayer: Holy are you, eternal King and giver of all holiness +. Holy is your only-begotten Son,
our Lord Jesus Christ; holy is your Holy Spirit, the Lord and Giver of life, who searches all things, even the depths of your Godhead.
Here let him bow. Holy are you, Almighty and all-powerful, awesome and good.
Truly holy are you, who were merciful above all to your creature, who created man from the earth in your image and likeness and granted him the delight and rest of paradise,
so that he might have dominion over the creatures that were made by you and govern the world with dignity and righteousness.
But when he transgressed your commandments, he was cast out from there; yet you did not disregard him, nor did you cast him away, O Good One,
but you instructed him as a merciful father, and called him through the Law, and became his nurturer through the prophets.
And after them, at the last end of [?] the times of the ages, you sent your only-begotten Son himself into the world,
so that he might renew and restore your image. He came down from heaven and became incarnate of the Holy Spirit and of Mary, the Mother of God and ever-virgin,
was born in Bethlehem of Judea, was baptized in the holy Jordan by John, and lived among men.
And he ordered all things for the salvation of our race.
And when he, the life-giving and sinless one, was about to submit and willingly take death upon himself for us sinners, on that night
in which our Lord Jesus Christ was handed over for the whole world, he took the bread in his holy, spotless and incorruptible hands, lifted it up and showed it to you, God and Father.
He gave thanks +. Amen. He blessed it +. Amen. He sanctified it +. Amen. He broke it and gave it to his own disciples, the apostles, and said to them:
Exclamation: Take and eat, for this is my body, which is broken for you and for many and given for the forgiveness of sins +.
People: Amen.
Priest: In the same way, after supper, he took the cup, mixed with wine and water, in his holy and undefiled hands, lifted it up and showed it to you, God and Father.
He gave thanks +. Amen. He blessed it +. Amen. He sanctified it +. Amen. He filled it with the Holy Spirit and gave it to his blessed disciples and apostles, and said to them:
Aloud: Drink of this, all of you, for this is my blood of the new covenant, which is shed and given for you and for many for the forgiveness of sins +.
People: Amen.
Priest: Do this in remembrance of me. As often as you eat this bread + and drink this cup +,
you proclaim the death of the Son of Man + and confess his resurrection, until he comes.
And now we remember his sufferings, his burial and his resurrection on the third day, his ascension into heaven, and at your right hand, O God and Father,
his sitting, and his second, terrible coming in glory, when he comes to judge the living and the dead, when he will repay each and every person according to their deeds.
Here he bows. Remember us, O Lord our God, on that day: me and this people standing here to make supplication to you, O Lord.
We offer, O Lord, this awesome and bloodless sacrifice, so that you may not deal with us according to our sins or repay us according to our iniquities,
but according to your forbearance and your endless love for humankind, overlook and blot out whatever sins and errors your supplicants have committed.
And grant and bestow upon us those heavenly, eternal gifts which eye has not seen, nor ear heard, nor have entered into the heart of man, which in your mercy you have prepared for those who love you.
Aloud: For your people, O Lord, and your church entreat you.
People: Have mercy on us, O God, Father Almighty.
The priest shall say: Have mercy on us, O God, Father Almighty +. Have mercy on us, O God our Savior +. Have mercy on us, O God,
according to your great mercy +, and send down upon us and upon this awesome and bloodless sacrifice set forth here, this holy offering,
your Holy Spirit, the Lord and Giver of life, who shares the throne with you the Father and with the Son, who reigns with you and is co-eternal,
equally without beginning and of one being with you, who spoke in the Law, in the Prophets and in the New Covenant,

who came down upon our Lord Jesus Christ at the river Jordan in the form of a dove, and who came down upon the holy apostles in the likeness of tongues of fire in the upper room of the Mystery in the days of Pentecost.
Send down this same all-holy Spirit of yours, O Lord, upon us and upon this offering that lies here,
Aloud: so that now, by his good and glorious coming, he may sanctify this bread + and make it the precious body of Christ.
People: Amen.
Priest: And this cup + the true blood of Christ.
People: Amen.
The priest shall begin the mysteries: so that they may be [?] for all who receive them +, for the forgiveness of sins and for eternal life +,
for the cleansing of souls and bodies, for the bringing forth of the fruit of good works +, for the strengthening of your church,
which you acquired with the precious blood of your Christ and founded upon the rock of faith, so that the gates of hell should not prevail against it;
and deliver it from all heretics and from the stumbling-blocks of those who work lawlessness, until the end of the age, for its sake [?].
Here the priest bows. + And we offer to you, Lord, this awesome and bloodless sacrifice for your holy places, which you glorified by the manifestation of your Christ.
First, for holy and glorious Zion, the mother of all churches,
and for your holy catholic and apostolic church throughout the whole world and to all the ends of the heavens; abundantly increase upon it the gifts of the Holy Spirit, Lord.
Remember, Lord, in it our holy fathers, the bishops, who are orthodox and rightly proclaim the word of truth:
first and foremost our venerable father the patriarch; grant him an honorable old age,
preserve him with long life for these times as shepherd of your people in all truth and righteousness and holiness.
Remember, Lord, the holy city of Jerusalem and all cities and villages, and all
who dwell in them in faith and in the fear of Christ, in peace and tranquility.
Remember, Lord, here the honorable priests, and also [?] the deacons who serve Christ, and all the orders of the churches, and those who live a life of humility, and the Christ-loving laypeople.
Remember me also, Lord, this sinful and worthless servant of yours, and look upon me with your mercy, and keep me blameless before my persecutors; and whatever I have sinned against you in word,
or in deed, or in thought, have mercy on me, remit it, forgive me, for you are a good God and a Lord who loves mankind.
Lord, do not [?] in long-suffering, for where sin has abounded, there your gifts have abounded all the more.
Remember, Lord, our pious king and pious queen and their pious reign.
Take up weapon and shield and rise up to help them, and subject to them all the nations of the heathen, so that we may live in peace and quiet in all godliness and dignity.
Remember, Lord, those who toil in old age and infirmity: our fathers and brothers.
Remember also those who are in prison and in bonds and in exile and in captivity and in the caves of the earth: our fathers and brothers.
Remember, Lord, those who travel by ship and the wayfarers who are journeying in foreign lands and on long roads: our fathers and brothers, who ask mercy and help from you.
Remember, Lord, those who are tormented by unclean spirits; set free all the sick and the suffering and those who are oppressed;
have mercy on all, free all from diseases of every kind:
our fathers and brothers and all Christian souls who are afflicted and sorrowful, who ask for your mercy and help.
Remember all for good, Lord; have mercy on all in all things, Lord; look upon all; bring peace to the multitude of your people,
scatter all stumbling-blocks, put an end to all wars, and grant us your peace and love, our Savior.
The priest is to make the sign of the cross over the deacon, and the deacon is to say the commemoration of the living.
The priest is to say this prayer: Remember, Lord, the good tempering of the air, the peaceful dew,
the good, full and fine yielding of the fruits, and the crown of the year with your goodness, Lord; for the eyes of all wait upon you, and you give them their food in due season.
Remember, Lord, those who offered this offering [?] on this day at your holy altar,
and those for whom each one offered it, or whom they had in mind, and those for whom we now read aloud.
Here remember whichever of the living you wish.
Remember, Lord God, and have mercy on John Zosimus, the very sinful, the scribe of this, and Cyricus, its donor,
and their parents and brothers, and all who belong to them, each one by name, spiritual and bodily, living and dead, and all Christians. Amen. Pray.
Remember all of these, Lord, God of the fathers and of all flesh, both those we have remembered and those we have not been able to remember.

Give them the heavenly in place of the earthly, the incorruptible in place of the corruptible, the eternal in place of the temporal, according to the gospel of your Christ, for you have power over life and death, Lord.
And make us worthy also to remember those who from the beginning of the world have pleased you, generation after generation: the patriarchs,
prophets, apostles, evangelists, martyrs, the righteous, and confessors.
Remember, Lord, the voice of the archangel, who said: Hail, full of grace, the Lord is with you.
Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb, by the grace of God.
Aloud: Especially our all-holy, glorious, blessed, incorruptible, most blessed Lady, the Mother of God and ever-virgin Mary.
From here on the deacon is to commemorate the souls, while the priest says: Hail, full of grace, the Lord is with you. Three times.
Remember, Lord, the holy and glorious blessed John, the Forerunner and Baptist. Remember, Lord, the holy apostles:
Peter, Paul, Andrew, James, John, Philip, Thomas, Bartholomew, Matthew, James son of Alphaeus, Simon the Zealot, Judas son of James, Matthias, Mark, and Luke the evangelists.
Remember, Lord, the holy prophets and the righteous patriarchs: holy Stephen, the first deacon and first martyr,
our holy and blessed fathers Moses, Aaron, Joshua, Samuel, David, Elijah, Elisha, Zechariah, Simeon, and the holy martyrs and confessors of Christ our God:
Saint Theodore, Saint George, Saint Cyricus, Saint Julitta, Saint Abo, and the Holy Forty,
who were martyred with a good confession, and the holy women who made a good confession, the ointment-bearers, the myrrh-bearers.
Remember, Lord, our holy fathers the bishops: from holy James the apostle, brother of the Lord and first archbishop of Jerusalem, until now,
and those worthy ones who served as bishops in orthodoxy in the holy city of Christ our God.
Remember, Lord, our holy fathers the teachers: Ignatius, Dionysius, Irenaeus, Gregory, Alexander, Eustathius, Athanasius, Basil, Gregory, Gregory, Ambrose,
Amphilochius, Liberius, Damasus, John, Epiphanius, Theophilus, Celestine, Augustine, Cyril, Leontius, Proclus, Philistus [?], Hormisdas, Ephrem, Sophronius, Agapius, Eulogius, Martyrius.
Remember, O Lord, the holy and great six councils of the world: the three hundred and eighteen of Nicaea, the one hundred and fifty of Constantinople, the two hundred of the first council of Ephesus,
the six hundred and thirty of Chalcedon, the one hundred and sixty-four of the fifth holy council, and after it the two hundred and eighty-nine of the sixth holy council.
Remember these holy councils, and our worthy fathers in every place who served as bishops in orthodoxy and who rightly taught the word of truth.
Remember, O Lord, our holy fathers, the hermits and those who lived in solitude: Abba Paul, Antony, Paul, Pachomius, Ammon, Theodore, Hilarion, Arsenius,
Macarius, Macarius, John, Ephrem, Symeon, Symeon, Theodosius, Chariton, Gelasius, Euthymius, Theoctistus, Sabas, Dometius, Gerasimus, Cosmas [?] and John.
And our holy fathers who were killed by barbarians for Christ's sake on the holy mountain of Sinai and at Raithu.

It is not that we are worthy to commemorate their blessedness. We remember them so that they, standing boldly before your terrible and awe-inspiring throne, may remember us, your pitiable and unworthy servants.
Remember, O Lord, the chorepiscopi, priests, deacons, subdeacons, deaconesses, readers, monks, interpreters,
exorcists, God-loving virgins and those who were lawfully married, who have died in the communion of the Holy Spirit within the catholic and apostolic Church.
Remember, O Lord, the pious and faithful emperors:
Constantine, Helena, Theodosius the Great, Marcian, Pulcheria, Leontius, Justinian, and those who reigned piously and faithfully after them.
And all the Christ-loving laypeople who have died before us in faith and in the fear of Christ.
And those for whom each person has made an offering or whom they have in mind, and those whose names we now read out.
Remember whichever of the departed you wish.
Remember, O Lord God, have mercy on and give rest to the soul of John the sinner, and of Zosimas and Cyricus, and of their parents and brothers
and all who belong to them, spiritual and bodily, each one by name, and all Christians. Amen. Pray.
O Lord, God of the fathers and of all flesh, remember all these: those we have named and those we have not been able to name.
Give them rest there and make them worthy of the land of the living, the kingdom of heaven, in the bosom of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob,
from which all pain, sorrow and distress have fled away, where the light of your face looks upon them, O Lord.
And guide our end to be Christian and peaceful, without sin, without grief, without distress and without shame, O Lord God, our Savior,
and gather us under the wings of your chosen ones, whenever you wish and in whatever way you wish, only without shame or disgrace, before the throne of your Christ.

Deacon: And for peace and the good order of the whole world and of the holy churches of God, and for each one of these, and for those for whom each person has made an offering or whom they had in mind, and for all the people standing here, for all and for everything.
People: For all and for everything.
Priest: By the grace, mercy and love for mankind of your Christ, with whom glory is fitting to you, together with the Holy Spirit +, now and always and to the ages of ages.
People: Amen.
Priest: Peace to all.
People: And with your spirit.
Deacon: Again, all together, let us pray to the Lord.
People: Kyrie eleison.
For this holy, offered, sanctified, glorious heavenly gift, let us pray to the Lord.
People: Kyrie eleison.
That the Lord our God, who has accepted these upon his holy, invisible, glorious and heavenly altar as a sacrifice of sweet-smelling fragrance,
may send down upon us the grace and gift of the Holy Spirit, all together let us pray to the Lord.
People: Kyrie eleison.
Let us ask of the Lord the unity of the faith and the communion of the all-holy Spirit, and let us commend ourselves and our whole life to Christ our God.
People: To you, O Lord.
The priest shall say this prayer: O God and Father of our Lord God and Savior Jesus Christ, you who sit upon the cherubim and are glorified by the seraphim,
before whom stand thousands of thousands and myriads of myriads of holy angels and the hosts of the archangels: these offerings that have been offered + to you,
and the gifts to be given, and the fruits, accept them as a sweet-smelling fragrance and sanctify them, O Lord, by the grace of your Christ and by the coming of your Holy Spirit.
Sanctify, O Lord, our souls and bodies, examine our minds, test our thoughts, and remove from us every [?] mind of wickedness and every defiled thought,
and every filthy desire, and all envy, and all pride, and all double-mindedness, and every lie and deceit,
and every burden of this world, and all greed, and every impulse of the flesh and of the spirit that is estranged from your holy will.
Aloud: And make us worthy, O Lord, with boldness, with a pure heart, a renewed spirit, an unashamed face +,
and sanctified lips + to dare to call upon you, the God of heaven, holy and merciful Father, and to say:
People: Our Father... + + +
The priest shall say this prayer: And lead us not into temptation, O Lord, Lord, God of hosts,
but deliver us from the evil one and from his works, for the sake of your holy name, which has been called upon us in our lowliness.
Aloud: For yours is the kingdom, the power and the glory, of the Father and of the Son + and of the Holy Spirit, now and always and to the ages of ages.
People: Amen.
Priest: Peace to all.
People: And with your spirit.
Deacon: Let us bow our heads to the Lord.
People: To you, O Lord.
The priest shall say this prayer: Your servants and handmaids bow the necks of their hearts to you, and ask for the spiritual gift that comes from you.
Send down your blessing, O Lord, and sanctify our souls, our spirits [?] and our bodies,
so that we may become worthy to partake of your incorruptible heavenly mysteries, for the forgiveness of our sins and as provision for the journey to eternal life.
Exclamation: For you are our God, worshipped and glorified, + together with your only-begotten Son and your all-holy Spirit, now and always and to the ages of ages.
People: Amen.
The priest shall say: May the grace + of the holy and consubstantial + and worshipful Trinity + be with you all.
People: And with your spirit.
Deacon: Attend.
The priest shall lift up the prosphora and say this prayer: Ineffable God, Word of the Father and of the Holy Spirit, coessential, co-principal, co-reigning and co-existent,
accept from us the hymn of the holy and bloodless sacrifice, the unceasing hymn sung with the cherubim and seraphim, the word proclaimed aloud by me, a sinner and your unworthy servant.
Prayer 2. Holy, Holy One, who are glorified and who rest among the holy, O Lord: sanctify us by the word of your grace and by the coming of your Holy Spirit,
for you, O Lord, have said: 'Be holy, for I am holy, the Lord your God.'
The priest shall lift the prosphora up high and say: The Holy Things for the holy.
People: One is holy, one is Lord, Jesus Christ, [?] of God the Father, with the Holy Spirit, to whom belongs glory to the ages of ages. Amen.
The priest shall say this prayer: In faith + [?] for building up and strengthening. And [he may name] anyone else he wishes, living or reposed.
People: Kyrie eleison, fifteen times.
Then the priest shall break the prosphora, make the sign of the cross three times with one half, and put it into the chalice. Over the blood he shall make the sign of the cross three times, saying:
"The body and blood of Christ are united, in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit." With the one half he shall make the sign of the cross over the other half,
take that half in his right hand and do the same, join the edges crosswise [?], and make the sign of the cross three times over the paten.
And if other prosphora is also lying on the paten, he shall make the sign of the cross over all of it with it,
…let him dip it into the blood, break it into four, and break off two pieces (literally "two eyes"). With it let him make the sign of the cross over the chalice and say this three times.
Let him say: The Body and Blood of Christ are united, sanctified and perfected, in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit.
Let him place it in the chalice and say: Blessed is the Father, blessed is the Son, blessed is the Holy Spirit.
Let every soul and every creature praise the Lord. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.
Let the deacon say: In the peace of Christ let us sing.
The people shall say "Taste [and see]," while the priests and deacons shall say Psalm 33 during this distribution [?].
[?] I will bless the Lord at all times; his praise shall be always [in my mouth]. [Continue] as far as "Blessed is the man who hopes in the Lord."
Then the priest shall say this prayer, spoken by Saint Athanasius, bishop of Alexandria:
O Lord God, lover of mankind and Redeemer, Jesus Christ, Son of the living God, who appeared in the flesh as our Saviour and enlightened the whole world,
you have done very great wonders and mercies for us, so that you might set us completely free from slavery to death.
You, the holy and spotless Lamb of God, appeared for our sake in human nature, and like a sheep
you were led to the slaughter in your precious flesh and your true blood. You, the Righteous One, were crucified among thieves as though you were an evildoer.
Yes, O Lord, before your crucifixion you took bread in your holy and spotless hands, blessed it and gave it to your blessed disciples, and said:
"This is my body." After the supper you took the cup, mixed with wine and water, in your holy and spotless hands.
You blessed it and gave it to those same blessed disciples, the apostles, and said: "This is the blood. Do this in remembrance of me,
for as often as you eat this bread and drink this cup, you proclaim the death of the Son of Man until he comes."
Now we remember that blessing and your commandment. But as for me, if only I had that spiritual shame for my most grievous sins and abominations,
I am not worthy even to look up. But to you alone I say in confession:
I have sinned, O Lord. O Lord, I have sinned, and I know my iniquities. I dare to approach this ineffable mystery unworthily and presumptuously,
your precious body and your true blood. But in faith I have hope in your incomprehensible mercy and sweetness,
and I ask of you, our Lord Jesus Christ: have mercy on me, O Lord. O Lord, have mercy on me, and do not condemn me for my unworthy presumption.
Instead, let this holy and true body and blood of yours be for me the stripping away of my sins, the blotting out of my iniquities and the enlightening of the eyes of my mind,
so that I may be cleansed from great sin, may fear you always, and may flee from all sin and impurity,
and may long all the more for this precious body and true blood of yours, and may always speak in my heart of the kingdom of heaven,
for yours is the kingdom, the power and the glory, together with the Father and the Holy Spirit, now and always and to the ages of ages. Amen.
Prayer of Communion of John Chrysostom. Through this Body I am no longer earth and ashes, nor am I dust any longer, but free.
Through this I hope to receive in the heavens the good life, the immortal glory of the angels, and converse with Christ.
Another prayer of Communion. Holy, holy, ineffable and gracious Trinity, grant me to receive this Body and Blood for salvation, and not for torment and condemnation,
nor for the increase of sins; but grant me fruit pleasing to you, so that I may appear pleasing to you and be saved by keeping your commandments,
and that I may boldly call upon you, God, as Father, and seek your name and your will. Hallowed be your name upon us forever, O Lord.
For you are mighty, and praised and glorified is your holy name, of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, now and always and to the ages of ages. Amen.
The priest shall take a portion, two particles (literally "pearls"), in his hands, touch it to his mouth three times [?], and say this:
I will exalt you, my God and my King, and I will bless you. This three times. I believe in the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit. Let him say this three times.
I believe in the Annunciation, the Nativity, the Baptism, the Crucifixion, the Burial, the Resurrection, the Ascension into heaven, and the Second Coming in glory to judge the living and the dead.
[?] ("ia ib") But for me, drawing near to God is good, to put my hope in the Lord.
And let him communicate first of the Body and then of the Blood.
The deacon shall say: Priests, come forward! Deacons, let us approach! The deacon shall lift up the paten and say "Kyrie eleison."
The priest: I will exalt you, my God.
The priest: Peace to all. +
The people: And with your spirit.
The deacon: With the fear of Christ let us approach.
The people: Before you, O Lord.
At Communion, when the priest gives Communion to priests, let him say this: The Body and the all-holy Blood of the Lord God and our Saviour Jesus Christ,
the Son of God, is given to the priest of Christ our God, to keep your priesthood in worthiness and holiness, for the forgiveness of sins and for eternal life.
For deacons he says the same, changing only the title. For the people let him say this:
The Body and Blood of the Lord God and our Saviour Jesus Christ is given to you for the forgiveness of sins and for eternal life.

And when they have communicated, the priest shall make the sign of the cross over the people and say: You are exalted in the heavens, O God, and your glory is over all the earth. And they take up [the response]: We thank you, O Lord.
The deacon, the litany: Stand upright, we who have received this holy, glorious, life-giving, heavenly, incorruptible,
life-creating mystery of our Lord Jesus Christ; let us all together give thanks to the Lord our God.
The people: We thank you, O Lord.
that this holy [gift] which we are to receive may be for us for salvation and for trampling down our enemy,
for the forgiveness of our sins, through the reception of the Holy Spirit, let us all together pray to the Lord.
People: Kyrie eleison.
Our all-holy, glorious, blessed, incorruptible, most blessed Lady, the Mother of God and ever-virgin Mary, all the saints,
the righteous and the martyrs let us commemorate; let us commend ourselves and our whole life to Christ our God.
People: To you, O Lord.
The priest shall say this prayer: O God, who in your great mercy forgive the weakness of your servants,
make us worthy to receive from this heavenly altar, and do not condemn us sinners
through the receiving of your incorruptible mysteries, but keep us, O good Lord, in your holiness and righteousness,
so that we may become worthy and partakers with your Holy Spirit, and may find a portion of inheritance and grace with all your saints in the light of your face, through the mercy of your Christ.
Exclamation: For blessed and holy and glorious is your all-honourable and most magnificent name, of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, now and always and to the ages of ages.
People: Amen.
Priest: Peace to all.
People: And with your spirit.
Deacon: Our heads [?]
People: To you, O Lord.
The priest shall say this prayer: O God, who are great and wonderful, look upon your servants, for we have bowed our heads to you.
Stretch out, for the salvation of the human race, your almighty hand and your exalted arm, which is full of blessing, and save your people and bless
your inheritance, so that at all times we may bless you, the only living and true God, the holy Trinity, consubstantial, the holy Trinity.
Exclamation: For to you, from all, is due the offering of glory, honour and worship, Father and Son and Holy Spirit, now and always and to the ages of ages.
People: Amen.
Let all say three times: Blessed be the name of the Lord from henceforth and forevermore.
Deacon: Let us keep ourselves in the peace of Christ.
People: In the name of the Lord, O Lord, bless us.
The priest shall pray, make the sign of the cross, turn back to the altar, and say: Glory to the Father and to the Son and to the Holy Spirit, now and always and to the ages of ages. Amen.
The deacon: Let us pray to the Lord.
The people: Kyrie eleison.

The priest says this prayer: Those whom you have called, those whom you have sanctified, O Lord, those whom you have glorified, O Lord, make us worthy of the heavenly calling; keep us in love and establish us in your holiness;
guard us from evil and gather us into eternal life, and make us worthy of your mercy, and grant us every request that is needful for us.
Keep us under the shelter of your goodness [?] and deliver us at all times,
so that we may be pleasing to you and do your will, by the grace and mercy and love for humankind of Christ, your only-begotten Son,
with whom you are blessed, together with your all-holy, good and life-giving Holy Spirit, now and always and to the ages of ages. Amen.
The priest: Peace to all. The people: And with your spirit. Lord, bless us.
The priest turns around and says this prayer of the dismissal of the people: We have been filled with the good things of your house and with abundance, and now we entreat you,
O Lord: in your perfect love make our souls worthy of the light of your face.
Guard our ways and establish them in the fear of you, and have mercy on all of us, and make us, unworthy as we are, worthy of the heavenly kingdom.
For blessed is your name and the glory of your kingdom, that the might of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit may be glorified, now and always and to the ages of ages. Amen.
When the priest goes into the diaconicon, the deacons go before him. The priest says this: By the intercession of the victors of your contest, O Christ, have mercy on us.
Glory to the Father and to the Son and to the Holy Spirit, now and always and to the ages of ages. Amen.
Holy are you, holy are you, holy are you, O Lord; glory to you. Let us pray to the Lord.
The people: Kyrie eleison.
Let us commemorate Saint Stephen, the first deacon and first martyr, and all the saints, the righteous and the martyrs, so that through their intercession the Lord may have mercy on us.
The people: Kyrie eleison.
Then the priest takes off his vestments. He says this prayer: For grant us, O Lord, holiness and a share of the holy body and the true blood of your Christ;
grant us also, O Lord, the grace of your Holy Spirit; keep us blameless in faith, and lead us to attain to all perfection,
and make us worthy of the eternal rest to come, by the grace and mercy and love for humankind of your Christ,
with whom glory befits you, together with the Holy Spirit, now and always and to the ages of ages. Amen.
Prayer 2: Blessed is [?] God, who has blessed us and sanctified us and kept the life of all of us through the partaking of his immaculate,
holy, life-giving, heavenly, immaculate mysteries; who is blessed to the ages of ages. Amen.
Prayer at the time of the gathering-up [?]: We thank you, O Lord, eternal Light, giver of gifts, who cares for souls, leader of the saints,
Give us eyes of understanding, so that we may see you, and ears that listen to you alone, so that our souls may be filled with your grace,
and establish a pure heart within us, Lord, so that we may be established in your steadfastness and holiness, wondrous God who loves humankind.
Adorn our souls and calm our minds, unchangeably, which we, your servants who give you thanks, have received from your grace,
for blessed is your kingdom and your glory, of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, now and always and to the ages of ages. Amen.
Pray.
The liturgy is ended.
Christ, have mercy on John, the copyist of this. Pray. Amen.
Holy priests of Christ, who serve with these liturgies: for God's sake, entrust to your holy prayers John, the copyist of this, a great sinner,
and my parents and brothers and all who are mine, living and dead, for I firmly trust in your prayers. And may Christ receive you too. Amen.
Holy fathers, forgive me: the exemplar of this liturgy was missing many rubrics, prayers and words, from beginning to end,
as I knew from my teachers were written in the liturgies, and I was not at all happy about it.
But the one who had me write it begged me earnestly, saying: "Write for me only what is written in that copy."
So I have copied only that, with great reluctance, for God's sake. Do as you see fit, but always remember me in your holy prayers.
This liturgy was written at Holy Sinai by the hand of John Zosimus, a great sinner, in the days of my wretched old age, for prayers on behalf of me and all who are mine,
when the years from the creation of the world were, by the Georgian reckoning, 6589, and the chronicon was 205. Now I beg you again: for God's sake, forgive me all my shortcomings,
and remember in your holy prayers me, a great sinner, and all those written above. And may Christ have mercy on all of you together. Amen.
